question.text: Besides the court's penalty, in what four ways can a traffic conviction cost you your license?

answer.text: On top of whatever the court imposes, a conviction for breaking a traffic law can cost you your license through cancellation, revocation, suspension or disqualification.

teaching.text: A court penalty is not the end of it: the same conviction can also cost the license through cancellation, revocation, suspension or disqualification. Remember: cancel, revoke, suspend, disqualify.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On top of whatever the court imposes, a conviction for breaking a traffic law can cost you your license through cancellation, revocation, suspension or disqualification.

question.text: What does it cost at minimum to be relicensed after losing your license?

answer.text: Getting relicensed after a cancellation, suspension, revocation or disqualification requires a reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars plus any other state-law requirements.

teaching.text: However the license was lost, coming back starts with a reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars, plus any other legal requirements. Remember: at least one hundred dollars.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Getting relicensed after a cancellation, suspension, revocation or disqualification requires a reinstatement fee of at least one hundred dollars plus any other state-law requirements.

question.text: What extra fee applies if you do not surrender your license in time?

answer.text: Failing to surrender your license within the allowed time after it is canceled, revoked or suspended adds a fifty dollars fee.

teaching.text: Turn the license in on time after it is taken; a late surrender adds fifty dollars to the bill. Remember: late surrender, fifty more.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to surrender your license within the allowed time after it is canceled, revoked or suspended adds a fifty dollars fee.

question.text: What extra reinstatement fees follow a drug conviction or a child-support suspension?

answer.text: Reinstatement after a drug-related conviction costs an extra twenty-five, dollars and reinstating after a suspension for unpaid child support costs an extra fifty dollars.

teaching.text: Two causes add their own charges: twenty-five dollars after a drug-related conviction and fifty dollars after a child-support suspension. Remember: drugs twenty-five, support fifty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reinstatement after a drug-related conviction costs an extra twenty-five, dollars and reinstating after a suspension for unpaid child support costs an extra fifty dollars.

question.text: How do the reinstatement fee and its extra charges add up?

answer.text: Every reinstatement costs at least one hundred, dollars with fifty dollars more for a late license surrender, twenty-five dollars more after a drug conviction, and fifty dollars more after a child-support suspension.

teaching.text: Build the total from the base fee of at least one hundred dollars, then add fifty for a late surrender, twenty-five for drugs, fifty for child support. Remember: base hundred plus add-ons.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Every reinstatement costs at least one hundred, dollars with fifty dollars more for a late license surrender, twenty-five dollars more after a drug conviction, and fifty dollars more after a child-support suspension.

question.text: When may the ALEA Director cancel a license?

answer.text: The ALEA Director may cancel a license on finding the holder was not entitled to it, and missing or false application information or application fraud is also grounds for cancellation.

teaching.text: Cancellation is about entitlement: the Director may cancel when you were never entitled to the license, including false or missing application information. Remember: not entitled, so cancelled.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The ALEA Director may cancel a license on finding the holder was not entitled to it, and missing or false application information or application fraud is also grounds for cancellation.

question.text: What must a driver do once a revocation period ends?

answer.text: Once a revocation period ends, the driver may apply for a new license but must take and pass the complete examinations again.

teaching.text: When a revocation ends you start over, applying for a new license and passing every examination again. Remember: revoked means retest everything.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Once a revocation period ends, the driver may apply for a new license but must take and pass the complete examinations again.

question.text: How is getting a license after revocation different from cancellation?

answer.text: After revocation you must apply for a new license and pass the complete examinations, whereas after cancellation the issue is that you were never entitled to the license at all.

teaching.text: Revocation is followed by a new application and complete exams, while cancellation means the license should never have been issued. Remember: revoked retests, cancelled never entitled.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After revocation you must apply for a new license and pass the complete examinations, whereas after cancellation the issue is that you were never entitled to the license at all.

question.text: Which vehicle crimes force the Director to revoke a license?

answer.text: The Director must revoke a license after a conviction for manslaughter or homicide caused by operating a motor vehicle, or for using a motor vehicle to commit a felony.

teaching.text: Killing someone through driving, or using a vehicle in a felony, leaves the Director no choice but to revoke. Remember: killing or felony, revoked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The Director must revoke a license after a conviction for manslaughter or homicide caused by operating a motor vehicle, or for using a motor vehicle to commit a felony.

question.text: Which impaired-driving convictions make revocation mandatory?

answer.text: Revocation is also mandatory on a second or later conviction for driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle under the influence of alcohol, or for driving as a habitual user of, or while too impaired by, a controlled substance to drive safely.

teaching.text: Repeat impaired driving, by alcohol or a controlled substance, makes revocation mandatory. Remember: second impaired conviction, revoked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Revocation is also mandatory on a second or later conviction for driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle under the influence of alcohol, or for driving as a habitual user of, or while too impaired by, a controlled substance to drive safely.

question.text: Which conviction triggers mandatory revocation for impaired driving?

answer.text: Mandatory revocation for driving under the influence of alcohol is triggered by a second or subsequent conviction, and the same holds for controlled-substance impairment.

teaching.text: Count the convictions: a second or later impaired-driving conviction means mandatory revocation, while a first is a suspension ground. Remember: second time, not first.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Mandatory revocation for driving under the influence of alcohol is triggered by a second or subsequent conviction, and the same holds for controlled-substance impairment.

question.text: What crash behavior makes revocation mandatory?

answer.text: Failing to stop, give aid, or identify yourself after a crash that kills or injures another person is a mandatory revocation offense.

teaching.text: Leaving a crash that killed or hurt someone, without stopping, helping or identifying yourself, means mandatory revocation. Remember: hit, run, revoked.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to stop, give aid, or identify yourself after a crash that kills or injures another person is a mandatory revocation offense.

question.text: Which false statements, reckless driving streaks or vehicle misuse require revocation?

answer.text: Perjury or a false sworn statement to the Director about license or vehicle laws, three reckless driving convictions within twelve months, and unauthorized use of someone else's vehicle all require revocation.

teaching.text: Lying to the Director under oath, three reckless driving convictions in twelve months, and using someone's vehicle without permission all require revocation. Remember: three reckless in twelve months.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Perjury or a false sworn statement to the Director about license or vehicle laws, three reckless driving convictions within twelve months, and unauthorized use of someone else's vehicle all require revocation.

question.text: When may a license be suspended, and when is it not reinstated afterward?

answer.text: A license may be suspended after certain convictions or a finding of incompetence to drive, and it is reinstated afterward unless it expired meanwhile or the suspension requirements were not all met.

teaching.text: Suspension is a time out: the license normally comes back afterward, unless it expired or a requirement was missed. Remember: suspended, then usually back.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A license may be suspended after certain convictions or a finding of incompetence to drive, and it is reinstated afterward unless it expired meanwhile or the suspension requirements were not all met.

question.text: What two things can keep a suspended license from being reinstated?

answer.text: A suspended license is reinstated when the period ends, unless it expired during the suspension or the suspension requirements were not all met.

teaching.text: A suspended license returns when the period ends, but not if it expired meanwhile or the conditions were not all met. Remember: expired or unmet requirements.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A suspended license is reinstated when the period ends, unless it expired during the suspension or the suspension requirements were not all met.

question.text: Which driving-record problems are grounds for suspension?

answer.text: Suspension grounds include serious moving-violation convictions frequent enough to show disrespect for traffic laws, a record of habitually reckless or negligent driving, and incompetence to drive.

teaching.text: Your record can suspend you: frequent serious violations, a habit of reckless or negligent driving, or incompetence to drive. Remember: frequent, reckless or incompetent.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Suspension grounds include serious moving-violation convictions frequent enough to show disrespect for traffic laws, a record of habitually reckless or negligent driving, and incompetence to drive.

question.text: How can misusing the license itself lead to suspension?

answer.text: Allowing unlawful or fraudulent use of your license, mutilating it, or committing an offense in another state that would be grounds here can also lead to suspension.

teaching.text: The card itself matters, so letting others misuse it, damaging it, or an out-of-state offense that counts here can bring suspension. Remember: lend it, lose it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Allowing unlawful or fraudulent use of your license, mutilating it, or committing an offense in another state that would be grounds here can also lead to suspension.

question.text: Which police, racing and court-summons problems can bring suspension?

answer.text: Convictions for fleeing or trying to elude a police officer or for racing on highways can bring suspension, as can failing to answer a traffic summons on time or failing to pay.

teaching.text: Running from police, racing on highways, and ignoring or not paying a traffic summons are all grounds for suspension. Remember: flee, race, skip court.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Convictions for fleeing or trying to elude a police officer or for racing on highways can bring suspension, as can failing to answer a traffic summons on time or failing to pay.

question.text: Which young drivers can lose a license for leaving school?

answer.text: Drivers aged fifteen through eighteen who withdraw from school before graduating, under certain conditions, can have the license suspended.

teaching.text: Teens aged fifteen through eighteen who leave school before graduating can lose the license under certain conditions. Remember: quit school, lose license.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drivers aged fifteen through eighteen who withdraw from school before graduating, under certain conditions, can have the license suspended.

question.text: Which insurance, support and health matters are grounds for suspension?

answer.text: Failing to keep SR-twenty-two insurance when it is required, unpaid child support, and medical reasons are further grounds for suspension.

teaching.text: Missing required SR insurance, unpaid child support and medical reasons can also lead to suspension. Remember: SR insurance, support, medical.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to keep SR-twenty-two insurance when it is required, unpaid child support, and medical reasons are further grounds for suspension.

question.text: What point total and graduated-license record appear on the suspension list?

answer.text: The suspension list includes having four or more points on the driving record, or two or more moving violations while holding a Graduated Driver License.

teaching.text: The suspension list names four or more points, and separately two or more moving violations on a Graduated Driver License. Remember: four points or two violations.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The suspension list includes having four or more points on the driving record, or two or more moving violations while holding a Graduated Driver License.

question.text: Are the point ground and the graduated-license ground the same threshold?

answer.text: The suspension list names four or more points on the record or two or more moving violations on a graduated license as two separate grounds for suspension.

teaching.text: Treat the four-point ground and the two-violation graduated-license ground as two separate triggers. Remember: two separate suspension triggers.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The suspension list names four or more points on the record or two or more moving violations on a graduated license as two separate grounds for suspension.

question.text: Is a first-offense DUI or drug offense grounds for suspension?

answer.text: A first-offense DUI or drug offense, for a juvenile or an adult, is listed as grounds for suspension.

teaching.text: Even a first DUI or drug offense, for a juvenile or an adult, appears among the grounds for suspension. Remember: first offense, suspension ground.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A first-offense DUI or drug offense, for a juvenile or an adult, is listed as grounds for suspension.

question.text: Where must an offense happen for Alabama points to be charged?

answer.text: Alabama's point system suspends licenses on uniform grounds, and points are charged for listed offenses whether they happen in Alabama or elsewhere.

teaching.text: Points follow you across state lines, because listed offenses are charged whether they happen in Alabama or elsewhere. Remember: points count anywhere.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Alabama's point system suspends licenses on uniform grounds, and points are charged for listed offenses whether they happen in Alabama or elsewhere.

question.text: How many points does a non-revocation drinking and driving conviction carry?

answer.text: A conviction on a charge involving drinking alcohol and driving that did not require mandatory revocation carries six points.

teaching.text: An alcohol-related driving conviction that did not require mandatory revocation still lands six points on the record. Remember: alcohol charge equals six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A conviction on a charge involving drinking alcohol and driving that did not require mandatory revocation carries six points.

question.text: How many points do reckless driving and an Admin Per Se violation carry?

answer.text: Reckless driving or reckless endangerment with a motor vehicle carries six points, and an Admin Per Se violation also carries six points.

teaching.text: Reckless driving, reckless endangerment with a vehicle, and an Admin Per Se violation each sit at the top with six points. Remember: reckless six, per se six.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reckless driving or reckless endangerment with a motor vehicle carries six points, and an Admin Per Se violation also carries six points.

question.text: How many points do failing to yield and passing a stopped school bus carry?

answer.text: Failing to yield the right of way and passing a stopped school bus each carry five points.

teaching.text: Failing to yield and passing a stopped school bus share the five-point rung. Remember: yield or bus, five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to yield the right of way and passing a stopped school bus each carry five points.

question.text: How do the six-point offenses compare with failing to yield?

answer.text: Reckless driving and an Admin Per Se violation each carry six points, one more than failing to yield or passing a stopped school bus.

teaching.text: Six points sits exactly one rung above the five points for failing to yield or passing a stopped school bus. Remember: six beats five by one.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reckless driving and an Admin Per Se violation each carry six points, one more than failing to yield or passing a stopped school bus.

question.text: How do points for passing a stopped school bus compare with an emergency vehicle violation?

answer.text: Passing a stopped school bus carries five points, while an emergency vehicle violation carries two points.

teaching.text: The school bus offense costs five points, while an emergency vehicle violation costs only two. Remember: bus five, emergency two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing a stopped school bus carries five points, while an emergency vehicle violation carries two points.

question.text: How many points for driving on the wrong side, passing illegally or following too closely?

answer.text: Driving on the wrong side of the road or passing illegally carries four points, and following too closely carries three points.

teaching.text: Driving on the wrong side or passing illegally costs four points, and tailgating costs three. Remember: wrong side four, tailgate three.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Driving on the wrong side of the road or passing illegally carries four points, and following too closely carries three points.

question.text: How do the points for tailgating and work-zone violations compare with illegal passing?

answer.text: Following too closely and ignoring work-zone markers each carry three points, one less than illegal passing at four points.

teaching.text: Tailgating and ignoring work-zone markers both cost three points, one below illegal passing. Remember: three is one below four.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Following too closely and ignoring work-zone markers each carry three points, one less than illegal passing at four points.

question.text: How do the points for speeding change at twenty-six miles per hour over the limit?

answer.text: Speeding one to twenty-five miles per hour over the limit carries two points, but speeding twenty-six miles per hour or more over the limit carries five points.

teaching.text: Speed tiers matter: up to twenty-five miles per hour over is two points, but twenty-six or more over is five. Remember: twenty-six over jumps to five.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speeding one to twenty-five miles per hour over the limit carries two points, but speeding twenty-six miles per hour or more over the limit carries five points.

question.text: Which other offense carries the same points as speeding twenty-six or more over?

answer.text: Speeding up to twenty-five miles per hour over the limit costs two points, but twenty-six miles per hour or more over costs five points, the same as failing to yield.

teaching.text: Very fast speeding, twenty-six or more over, costs the same five points as failing to yield. Remember: fast speeding matches failing yield.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speeding up to twenty-five miles per hour over the limit costs two points, but twenty-six miles per hour or more over costs five points, the same as failing to yield.

question.text: How many points for disobeying construction or maintenance zone markers?

answer.text: Failing to obey construction or maintenance zone markers carries three points.

teaching.text: Construction and maintenance zone markers are not suggestions; ignoring them costs three points. Remember: work zone, three points.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to obey construction or maintenance zone markers carries three points.

question.text: Which control, lane, drinking, motorcycle and emergency vehicle offenses carry two points each?

answer.text: Inability to control the vehicle, an improper lane violation, drinking alcohol while operating a vehicle, improper motorcycle operation, and an emergency vehicle violation each carry two points.

teaching.text: Losing control, lane violations, drinking while operating, improper motorcycle use and emergency vehicle violations each cost two points. Remember: control and lanes cost two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Inability to control the vehicle, an improper lane violation, drinking alcohol while operating a vehicle, improper motorcycle operation, and an emergency vehicle violation each carry two points.

question.text: Which signal, turn, coasting and unsafe operation offenses carry two points each?

answer.text: Failing to signal or using the wrong turn signal, making an improper turn, coasting, and unsafe operation each carry two points.

teaching.text: Signal mistakes, improper turns, coasting and unsafe operation are two-point offenses too. Remember: signals and turns cost two.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Failing to signal or using the wrong turn signal, making an improper turn, coasting, and unsafe operation each carry two points.

question.text: What suspensions do twelve to twenty points within two years bring?

answer.text: Within a two-year period, twelve to fourteen points bring a sixty-day suspension, fifteen to seventeen points bring ninety days, and eighteen to twenty points bring one hundred twenty days.

teaching.text: Within two years, twelve points start a sixty-day suspension, and each later band of three points adds thirty days up to one hundred twenty. Remember: sixty, ninety, one twenty.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Within a two-year period, twelve to fourteen points bring a sixty-day suspension, fifteen to seventeen points bring ninety days, and eighteen to twenty points bring one hundred twenty days.

question.text: What suspensions do twenty-one or more points within two years bring?

answer.text: Within a two-year period, twenty-one to twenty-three points bring a one hundred eighty-day suspension, and twenty-four or more points bring three hundred sixty-five days.

teaching.text: At the top, twenty-one to twenty-three points within two years mean one hundred eighty days, and twenty-four or more mean a full year. Remember: one eighty days, then a year.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Within a two-year period, twenty-one to twenty-three points bring a one hundred eighty-day suspension, and twenty-four or more points bring three hundred sixty-five days.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: one eighty days, then a year

question.text: What are the shortest and longest point suspensions, and where do they start?

answer.text: The shortest point suspension, sixty days, starts at twelve points within two years, and the longest, three hundred sixty-five days, starts at twenty-four points.

teaching.text: The schedule runs from sixty days at twelve points to three hundred sixty-five days at twenty-four points. Remember: twelve starts short, twenty-four longest.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The shortest point suspension, sixty days, starts at twelve points within two years, and the longest, three hundred sixty-five days, starts at twenty-four points.

question.text: What hearing may a driver request after a suspension notice, and where?

answer.text: After receiving a suspension notice, a driver may ask for a pre-suspension or administrative hearing before an ALEA agent in the home county.

teaching.text: A suspension notice is not the last word; you may ask for a hearing before an ALEA agent in your home county. Remember: hearing in your home county.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: After receiving a suspension notice, a driver may ask for a pre-suspension or administrative hearing before an ALEA agent in the home county.

question.text: How do you request an administrative hearing?

answer.text: An administrative hearing can be requested in writing to Driver License Services or online.

teaching.text: Ask for the administrative hearing in writing to Driver License Services or through the online request. Remember: in writing or online.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An administrative hearing can be requested in writing to Driver License Services or online.
